messages:
maria: Thinking about trying a different format for the annual planning offsite this year — a short 'studio' style mix of lightning demos, focused problem rooms, and two deep-work cycles. Want to test if this yields clearer launch criteria and faster scope alignment. Who wants to own facilitation tracks and customer-ask prioritization?

sam: curious — what's the primary outcome we need to guarantee? decisions on top 3 initiatives + owners? or more of alignment and discovery?

emily: for me the win is: leave with concrete launch criteria per initiative (metrics + must-have vs nice-to-have). we should bake that into each problem room.

tariq: AV/network note: if we're doing concurrent rooms, we need breakout A/V tested and backup dongles. also better to cap room sizes at 8 for focus.

alex: love the experiment. practical ask: can we keep the first morning open for cross-team lightning demos (max 5m each) so everyone has shared context before problem rooms.

maria: yes — proposed rough agenda below. open to pushback.

maria: ```
Day 1 AM: Intros + lightning demos (90m)
Day 1 PM: Problem Rooms (2 x 60m) — each outputs: scope doc + launch criteria + owner
Evening: informal customer stories dinner (optional)
Day 2 AM: Initiative sizing + OKR alignment (120m)
Day 2 PM: Roadmap triangulation + concrete rollouts (120m)
```

sam: ok. who leads the "customer asks prioritization" problem room? we need someone who can push on tradeoffs with PM + sales.

emily: i can co-facilitate if we have a sales rep there — want someone from CS to pull in real blockers. @alex can you nudge sales?

alex: looping in sales lead in a slack DM after this. happy to coordinate.

maria: action items i want to lock before EOD Fri: 1) assign facilitators for each room, 2) collect 1-2 customer ask examples per facilitator, 3) doc with template for "scope + launch criteria".

devex-bot: calendar: Draft event created — "Offsite: Studio Format Experiment" 2 days, invites pending. Link: https://calendar.redwood.ai/event/abc123

emily: also — can we make a short prework doc so teams come prepared with tradeoff levers (latency/cost/security) for each ask? that'll make the problem rooms faster.

tariq: +1 prework. i'll add an AV checklist and backup Wi-Fi creds to the logistical doc.

sam: potential risk: some stakeholders expect a traditional roadmap presentation. need a 15m "how this works" explainer at the top to set expectations.

maria: good call. we'll open with a 10-15m framing session: goals, outputs, and decision authority.

alex: facilitator volunteers so far: emily (customer asks), sam (initiative sizing), maria (overall flow). looking for two more for problem rooms and someone to run the OKR sync.

emily: i'll take customer asks.

maria: tagging next steps list — please add your name to this thread if you can own a room or run the OKR session. also drop any hard constraints (travel, dates to avoid).

sam: my hard block: can't travel week of 1845021000 (family event).

tariq: ok if virtual? i can join half day in person, half remote.

maria: final note — let's treat this as an experiment. if it doesn't land, we'll revert next year. but if it yields clearer launch decisions faster, we should adopt elements permanently.

maria: final action: everyone who volunteers, copy this template into the shared doc and add 1-2 customer asks by Wed. link: https://docs.redwood.ai/offsite-prep/studio-template
